title: Spill / read / bash capture limits measured on this host

probes.what: bash tool stdout for `awk BEGIN{for(i=1;i<=20000;i++)print i}`
probes.conclusion: The bash layer truncates its own capture and spills the FULL text to a subprocess log. The head/tail the model keeps is 64,000 chars. This is NOT dsh-spill-policy; it happens before content ever reaches the tool result.

probes.what: run_code returning a 64,108-byte file via tools.write
probes.conclusion: The write result is small, so spill-policy (12500 estimated tokens) had nothing to retain. Replacing a large write result is not observable via spill; the policy is content-driven, not size-of-source driven.

probes.switch: run_code program calls tools.read on the 64,108-byte file
probes.conclusion: read returns a 2,000-line window and reports totalLines; the program received only 11,199 of 64,108 bytes. `limit` > 2000 is rejected ('limit must be less than or equal to 2000'). This is the real gap for a PTC program that must consume a whole artifact: iterate with offset, or use bash.

verdict: Spill storage itself is complete and permission-correct (dirs 0700, files 0600, per-session layout, full bytes on disk). The gaps are (a) the bash capture layer's own 64k truncation and (b) read's 2,000-line paging. Neither loses data — the full text is always on disk at the reported path — but a program must page or shell out to consume it.
